key_insight: Zero-shot LLMs improved the trade-off between positive predictive value and case yield for identifying interstitial lung disease (ILD), using claims, clinical notes, or both.
clinical_relevance: More accurate ILD identification could strengthen drug-safety research by reducing outcome misclassification that can obscure associations.
method: Evaluated 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes, adjudicated by two pulmonologists.
Compared 12 open-access LLMs with 20 published claims-based algorithms, without task-specific training.
Measured positive predictive value and yield, then modeled effects on drug-safety estimates and sample size.
evidence_signal: Claims-only Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% positive predictive value at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% at 4.9% for the highest-PPV claims algorithm.
watch_item: Results require external validation beyond this code-selected, single-health-system oncology cohort; projected drug-safety benefits were simulated, not observed.
paper_title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
